chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A boy who had stolen was brought to Ali (peace be upon him), so he scratched his fingers, then said:
But, if you were to repeat, I would cut these.
He said, then he said: 'But, it was not done except by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and myself.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do to demonstrate the penalty for theft according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) demonstrated the penalty for theft by scratching his fingers, stating that if the boy repeated the crime, he would cut them. He clarified that this action was performed only by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and himself, indicating their exclusive authority or practice in this specific judicial ruling. This hadith highlights the unique judicial prerogative (khass) of the Imams to apply hadd penalties directly, distinguishing their authority from general caliphs or judges who typically required witnesses and formal court procedures.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Razeyn who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a boy who had stolen, so he<sup>asws</sup> scratched his fingers, then said:
‘But, if you were to repeat, I<sup>asws</sup> would cut these’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, it was not done except by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and myself<sup>asws</sup>’.
